title: Getting started
desc: Install from Steam, first launch, and the one-screen layout.
text: user guide / getting started getting started install from steam, first launch, and the one-screen layout. first launch install & first run ikandy is a windows desktop app, installed through steam. no account beyond steam, no setup wizard: you can be visualizing system audio in under a minute. install open ikandy on steam and install it like any other steam app. launch it from your steam library. steam keeps it updated automatically. on first launch ikandy indexes the preset library and runs a background reactivity scan. this takes a few seconds and happens silently while you use the app. a short welcome walks you in, a one-time photosensitivity notice shows before anything flashes, and the ? on the console replays the guided tour whenever you want it. what it needs windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), 8 gb ram, 2 gb of free storage, an audio output device, and a directx 12 gpu with webgpu support (nvidia gtx 900 series, amd rx 400 series, or intel uhd 600 and newer). core visual playback runs locally and does not require a separate ikandy account. steam is used for installation and licensing; optional features such as provider-based ai, online metadata, and enabled diagnostics require an internet connection. details are in the privacy policy . fastest path to visuals start playing music in any app on your computer, then in ikandy pick now playing as the source. no setup, no auth: ikandy listens to whatever windows is currently playing and starts reacting immediately. the layout one screen, one console ikandy has one layout: the full screen is the stage, and a slim console bar lives at the bottom. everything routes through that bar. when you step up to performing, stage is a second surface built for the job, and the main window always shows a return button when stage has control. the console bar, left to right now playing : album art, track title, artist. click the art to open synced lyrics. the source pill under the title shows what is connected; click it to change sources. playback : play, pause, skip, volume, and a seek bar. works with spotify, musicbee, foobar2000, vlc, and system audio, subject to each source's capabilities. engine + presets : tabs pick the engine that is driving the stage: milkdrop , glsl , webgpu , spout , or image . arrows step through looks, browse opens the full library, and auto cycles on a dwell timer you set. vibe + output : the vibe popover shapes bloom, motion blur, and post intensity. the scenes popover switches hand-built scenes with a per-scene intensity control. the master audio popover sets how much bass, mid, and treble drive the visuals, with a mix control, a master intensity fader, and a god-rays toggle. output opens the logo overlay , and the lut control can auto-pick a color grade per scene or cycle grades per preset. view + settings : fullscreen, hide the console, the black or chrome theme, a knobs / sliders switch for how the board's controls render, multi-monitor output, and the gear for sources & settings. the ? replays the guided tour any time. popovers, not buried menus deep controls live in small popovers that open from the bar: vibe, scenes, master audio, and luts. the gear opens the one real modal, sources & settings , for connecting sources, themes, ui size, displays, and diagnostics. live level meters sit on the board itself so you can see the signal you are mixing. multi-monitor extra displays are outputs you route to. the output window can mirror the main view onto the displays you pick, each mirror with its own gain, or span one continuous canvas edge to edge across them (the titlebar hides so nothing interrupts the image). per-display checkboxes choose which monitors take part, and live wallpaper can claim any of them as a set-and-forget desktop. the tour is always current the app's built-in tour (the ? on the console) walks these zones live, on your build. if this page and your console ever disagree, trust the console. next → audio sources + controls

title: Audio sources + controls
desc: Now Playing, Spotify, MusicBee, foobar2000, VLC, per-app capture with Smart Auto, shuffle, and playlists.
text: user guide / audio sources + controls audio sources + controls now playing, spotify, musicbee, foobar2000, vlc, per-app capture with smart auto, shuffle, and playlists. audio sources connect your music ikandy can connect to five source modes. each one offers a different feature set depending on what its underlying api exposes. switching between them automatically pauses the previous one. 🎵 spotify ● works out of the box · no account connection spotify plays through windows media controls, the same lane as any modern media app. press play in spotify and ikandy picks up track info, album art when the app publishes it, and the transport controls windows exposes: play, pause, and skip. per-process capture can lock the visuals onto spotify's audio alone. there is nothing to connect: no sign-in, no developer app, no keys. ikandy has no spotify account integration; it reads what spotify publishes to windows on your machine. followed an older guide? earlier builds offered a separate spotify connection with a client id setup. that integration has been removed. nothing is required from you: play in spotify and ikandy follows automatically. 🐝 musicbee ● full features · mbxhub plugin connects through the user-installed mbxhub plugin. ikandy can read now-playing metadata and artwork, control playback, browse playlists, search, and use musicbee's shuffle and repeat modes. one-time setup download mbxhub from the official musicbee add-on page . extract the download and copy mb_mbxhub.dll and mbxhub.exe into musicbee's plugins folder. restart musicbee, then confirm mbxhub appears under edit → preferences → plugins . in ikandy, choose musicbee . leave host at 127.0.0.1 and port at 8080 unless you changed the mbxhub configuration, then click connect . connection check with musicbee and mbxhub running, open http://localhost:8080/docs . if the api documentation loads, the plugin is reachable; use the configured port if you changed it. plugin status mbxhub is currently published by its developer as release-candidate software. the plugin requires .net framework 4.8, and its companion shell requires the .net 8 desktop runtime. its api or setup may change; the official add-on page is authoritative. getting help questions about mbxhub itself (installing it, the plugin not loading, its settings) go to the mbxhub support thread on the musicbee forum . if mbxhub is running and ikandy still won't connect, see musicbee won't connect in troubleshooting. 🎧 foobar2000 ● full features · beefweb plugin for the audiophile crowd. connects via the foo_beefweb component: a rest/json api that exposes the full library. playlist browse with search, every shuffle mode foobar supports, transport, album art, lyrics. the most feature-complete source ikandy offers. one-time setup download and install foo_beefweb from github.com/hyperblast/beefweb/releases . in foobar2000: file → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control . tick enable http server (default port 8880 ). optionally set a password. click apply. in ikandy, choose foobar2000 , leave port at 8880 , enter the password if set, and click connect . foobar2000 → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control 📺 vlc ● standard · local http connects to vlc’s built-in web interface: play, pause, skip, shuffle on/off, album art, synced lyrics. no library browse; pick what to play in vlc, control playback in ikandy. one-time setup open vlc → tools → preferences . switch show settings to all . navigate to interface → main interfaces and tick web . expand main interfaces → lua , set a lua http password , and save. restart vlc. in ikandy, choose vlc , paste the password, and click connect . vlc → preferences → all → interface → main interfaces → web (ticked) custom port if port 8080 is taken, change it in the same vlc preferences pane. match it in ikandy's vlc settings. 🎙️ now playing ● basic · windows media controls · zero setup the general windows source. reads compatible apps that publish to windows media controls, including spotify, youtube music, apple music, browser tabs, and tidal. track info, available transport controls, and album art (when the app publishes it) follow the active source. no browse, no shuffle. how to use it start playing music in any app on your computer. in ikandy, click the source pill on the console and pick now playing . track info and transport light up within a second. ikandy shows or greys out individual buttons based on what the active source app actually supports. firefox needs a flag chrome and edge bridge html5 media session to windows media controls automatically. firefox doesn’t by default : open about:config , search media.hardwaremediakeys.enabled , set it to true , and restart firefox. 🎯 per-process capture ● audio isolation · settings → source capture audio from one specific app rather than the whole system mix. if you’re gaming while listening through spotify or musicbee, ikandy normally reacts to everything: game effects, discord pings, notification sounds, and music. per-process capture can lock on to the music app alone. how to use it start the app you want to capture (for example, spotify or musicbee) and play something. in ikandy, open settings (⚙) → source tab → per-process capture . click scan . ikandy lists every app currently producing audio, with its icon. click capture next to the app you want. the banner at the top of the section confirms which app is active. to stop, click stop in the banner. ikandy returns to system audio automatically. switching apps click capture on a different app while one is already active : ikandy switches cleanly with no confirmation dialog. the banner updates immediately. use cases react to spotify or musicbee only, ignoring game audio and discord capture a daw or audio editor output for a live mix visualization isolate browser tab audio when youtube is playing alongside other apps test a specific app’s audio routing without affecting the rest of the system requires a connected source first per-process capture shares the same audio graph as system audio. connect a supported source (spotify, musicbee, vlc, etc.) or click 🎤 reconnect audio once before using it: this initializes the audio context. after that, per-process capture works independently. one tab runs the connections connect, disconnect, and switch available sources from ⚙ → source : musicbee, foobar2000, vlc, spotify and other media apps through windows media controls, browser and system audio, plus the system-audio reconnect and your playlists. a source that still needs setup shows it on its row and routes you to the right place with one click. transport buttons a source cannot perform (some apps do not expose skip or seek) grey out with a hint instead of failing silently. and if you just have a file: drag an audio file onto ikandy and it plays it, no source setup at all. audio controls beyond picking a source, you shape how the audio drives the visuals. bass / mid / treble drive : boost or cut how much the low, mid, and high frequencies push the visuals, plus a mix control to blend. master intensity : one fat fader for overall visual intensity on the current engine, from calm to double strength. per-asset reactivity : each asset (like a logo overlay) has its own master audio-reactivity control. volume and transport : play, pause, skip, and volume for sources that support control. drop a file : drag a local audio file onto ikandy and it plays and visualizes it directly. shuffle + playlists shuffle follows the source. musicbee and foobar2000 expose their own shuffle, repeat, and playback-order modes, and the playlist panel loads supported-source playlists with search, so you can browse and play without leaving the visuals. apps that ride windows media controls, spotify included, keep their shuffle settings inside the app itself. ← previous getting started next → visualizers + presets

title: Visualizers + presets
desc: Five engines on one stage. The MilkDrop library, cycling, reactivity, and your own presets.
text: user guide / visualizers + presets visualizers + presets five engines on one stage. the milkdrop library, cycling, reactivity, and your own presets. visualizers five engines, one stage the engine tabs on the console pick what is driving the stage: milkdrop , glsl , webgpu , spout , or image . milkdrop is the deep preset library this page covers; glsl and webgpu run hand-built and imported scenes , spout turns a live feed into a source, and image layers fx shaders over a photo. milkdrop, reborn milkdrop presets are rendered by warpcore, ikandy’s own milkdrop engine, which carries forward code from jordan berg’s butterchurn under its mit licence. ikandy ships a deep preset library: the base collection, extra curated packs, and an image category that layers especially well over a background photo. cycling looks auto on the console cycles presets on a dwell timer you set: how many seconds each look holds before the next. the sliders icon next to it opens timing and blend controls; a longer blend morphs cinematically between looks, a short one cuts kinetic. auto-cycle draws from a shuffle bag, so every preset in the active pool plays once before any can repeat. reactivity on first launch ikandy quietly scores the library in the background while you use the app, classifying each preset as reactive, non-reactive, or image-texture. the results are cached. in the browser, the reactive filter narrows the pool to presets that visibly answer the music; if the scan has not finished, a run scan button is right there. there is also a reactivity master for the whole engine: turn it down and presets settle into calm ambient motion instead of going dark, turn it up and the beat drives harder. the browser browse opens the full library with thumbnails. hover any card for a live preview; click to load it on the stage immediately. scene cards preview from a cached clip the same way. tabs, favorites, hiding, flagging, and reordering are covered in library . your own presets in the browser, custom presets loads a folder of presets , merged alongside the bundled library and remembered across restarts. both formats work: classic milkdrop .milk files and butterchurn .json presets. ikandy converts .milk files itself when you pick the folder, and checks every preset before it joins your library, so there is no separate converter to run. anything that will not convert is reported rather than silently dropped. misbehaving presets some presets produce invalid values on modern gpus. ikandy skips broken or near-black presets automatically and remembers them, so the cycle keeps moving. anything questionable lands in the flagged tab for you to judge. ← previous audio sources + controls next → library: browse + manage

title: Library: browse + manage
desc: Nine tabs, search, maker pills, favorites, hide and flag, My Scenes, previews, saving, file types.
text: user guide / library: browse + manage library: browse + manage nine tabs, search, maker pills, favorites, hide and flag, my scenes, previews, saving, file types. one browser, nine tabs every visual in ikandy lives in one browser. the top tabs split it by kind, each with its own identity color: milkdrop , glsl , webgpu , spout , and images for your picture library, then my scenes for the things you have made, and the three curation tabs: favorites , hidden , flagged . find it fast search filters the grid as you type, with a one-tap clear. category tabs inside milkdrop narrow the pool: all, reactive (from the reactivity scan ), your custom presets, and more. maker pills filter milkdrop by preset author with one click; glsl and webgpu get the same artist pills for their scenes. random pulls one look from the current pool and drops you straight back on the stage. three densities : list, grid, and large. large keeps cards big enough to actually read. curate it star anything : every card carries a favorite star, the favorites tab and its count update live, and shuffle can be told to draw from favorites only. hide what you never want in rotation; flag what needs a second look. both get their own tabs, so nothing is ever lost. drag to reorder : every grid in the browser reorders by drag, and your order sticks. previews hover any milkdrop card and it live-renders in a preview popup. scene cards on the visual, webgpu, and spout tabs play a cached clip on hover instead, so previews stay instant. click any card to put it on the stage immediately. my scenes scenes you compose or generate land in my scenes. each card can be replayed, renamed, or deleted. imported presets start as pending; promote the keepers into your own custom category with one action. saving, editing, versions from the studio, save as new creates a fresh asset and overwrite updates the one you are editing. originals and templates are protected: they can only be saved as new, never overwritten, and a duplicate-name guard keeps two assets from colliding. file types the image library accepts png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, and svg, and feeds both backgrounds and the logo maker . shaders paste in as glsl or wgsl text, milkdrop presets load as either classic .milk files or butterchurn .json (ikandy converts .milk itself on import, so there is no separate converter to run), and ai scenes travel as .vis packages with their provenance intact. browse music and visuals together the sync button opens the preset browser and the playlist panel as a pair, so you can line up the next track and the next look side by side. ← previous visualizers + presets next → scenes

title: Scenes
desc: The hand-built scene library and how scenes differ from presets.
text: user guide / scenes scenes the hand-built scene library and how scenes differ from presets. custom scenes audio-reactive, built in-house scenes are direct audio-reactive engines written for ikandy, driven by real-time frequency analysis. where a milkdrop preset interprets a recipe of math, a scene is code that listens: the music literally makes the picture. a library across four runtimes the scene library has grown far past its first handful, and it spans four runtimes: glsl fragment scenes, canvas2d scenes, three.js scenes, and webgpu compute scenes when your gpu supports them. the range runs from classic spectrum work (flames, bars, sweeping rays) to deep-space flythroughs, gravitational lenses, particle trails, and heavy compute pieces. flight scenes even take a game controller: plug one in and fly . turning scenes on open the scenes popover from the console and pick a card; it plays immediately. every scene has an intensity control for how hard it answers the audio, and scenes that need more expose their own row of controls right there: tone knobs, a god-rays switch, a color-grade slot. the house rule audio drives light and color, never the camera. nothing on screen shakes to the beat; when a scene has a camera, it belongs to you or the autopilot. it is why ikandy stays watchable for hours. layering scenes sit over the milkdrop stage and over fx images. drop the milkdrop opacity in its settings popover to let a scene take center stage, or keep it high and blend the two. scenes and fx shaders run at the same time. make your own scenes you compose, import, or generate with ai land in my scenes , ready to replay, rename, or put in a rundown. ← previous library: browse + manage next → hdr + 4k

title: HDR + 4K
desc: True HDR on an HDR display, wide gamut on a P3 panel, and 10 bit recording. Every tier.
text: user guide / hdr + 4k hdr + 4k true hdr on an hdr display, wide gamut on a p3 panel, and 10 bit recording. every tier. light above white a normal screen stops at white. an hdr screen can go brighter than white, so a sun, a flare or a spark glows instead of flattening out. ikandy does this automatically once windows and the display are set up for it, and it tells you in plain words whether you are seeing it. set it up in windows, open settings, system, display , pick the hdr monitor and turn on use hdr . without this, windows hands ikandy a standard screen. in ikandy, open settings and the about tab. hdr output is on by default when an hdr display is detected. read the status line under the switch: it names exactly why the current frame is or is not in hdr, and which destinations are receiving it. hdr headroom sets how far highlights may rise above white: 1.5x, 2x, 3x or 4x. 2x suits most displays. try 3x or 4x on a bright panel and step back down if it feels like too much. the cap is 4x for viewing comfort. wide gamut output turns on by itself when the display reports display p3. leave it on: the sdr show presents in p3, colors stay exact on every display, and feeds and recordings stay srgb. on a 4k display, open the output tab and set visual quality to high or ultra so the gpu worlds render at the panel's native size. auto picks a tier from your gpu. hdr output and headroom apply on the next frame. turning hdr output on or off also changes the canvas format, and that part takes effect on the next launch. what stays hdr every engine finishes on one pipe. shader imports, compute worlds, milkdrop, wgsl scenes and video loops all enter the same chain, so god rays, the color grade and temporal aa look the same in hdr. supported hdr sources keep their range: pq and hlg png and avif files, jpeg gain map images, high bit depth video, windows screen capture and spout input. mirror and span map the finished frame for each display's own capability, so an hdr screen and an sdr screen beside it each get the right picture. wallpaper presents scrgb on an hdr display and a mapped sdr result elsewhere. spout offers a separate fp16 hdr sender beside the compatible sdr one. ndi output stays sdr: hdr ndi needs the separately licensed ndi advanced sdk. record in 10 bit in the output tab, under rolling replay, pick a recording dynamic range : sdr, sdr 10 bit, hdr pq or hdr hlg. sdr 10 bit writes 10 bit webm with bt.709 color from the full precision show frame, so smooth gradients keep 1024 levels instead of 256. the hdr options write 10 bit webm with bt.2020 color: pq for hdr mastering, hlg for broadcast workflows. changing the range restarts the replay buffer. if the encoder cannot do hdr, ikandy says so instead of silently writing sdr. comfort the photosensitivity warning says that hdr displays can present brighter than standard, and where the headroom control is. intensity all the way down keeps every visual calm at any headroom. tier note hdr output, wide gamut and 10 bit recording work at every tier, base included. the steam page is authoritative. ← previous scenes next → fx shaders

title: FX shaders
desc: Real-time post effects and the FX image pipeline.
text: user guide / fx shaders fx shaders real-time post effects and the fx image pipeline. fx real-time fx shaders fx is three layers deep in ikandy: living treatments over an image, a post chain over everything, and a play layer for your hands. fx images pick a background photo on the image engine and run a live treatment over it. the set covers weather and texture (rain, fog, heat haze, dust film), analog and broadcast decay (vhs warp, data corruption, hologram), and paint and material (ink bleed, watercolor, liquid metal, shatter, plasma arc). every treatment is audio-aware, and the library keeps growing. the post chain a multi-pass post chain runs over the whole show: bloom, chromatic aberration, grain, scanlines, vignette, and contrast, each on a live knob with its own status light, plus tone and lut color grading and a god-rays pass. beat-reactive particle bursts ride on top as their own layer. this is the finish that makes everything underneath read like one image. the play layer mouse fx and draw mode put the pointer in the show: click ripples, freehand drawing with adjustable width, and particle trails, all blended over the visuals without ever touching the camera. performance quality tiers (battery, standard, high, ultra) scale the render resolution and supersampling, so the same show runs right on a laptop on battery and on a desktop pushing a wall. ← previous hdr + 4k next → capture fx

title: Capture FX
desc: Run any app, game, window, Spout feed or video loop through effects that answer kick, snare and hats. Studio.
text: user guide / capture fx capture fx run any app, game, window, spout feed or video loop through effects that answer kick, snare and hats. studio. effects that need a feed the input tab of the library holds effects rather than standalone visuals. they run on top of video coming from somewhere else: a screen or window on this pc, a video file from your loop library, or another app such as obs, resolume, touchdesigner or madmapper. three ways in capture a screen or window. the quickest way in: point ikandy at any monitor, game or app window and the effect processes it live. native windows capture keeps hdr sources in hdr, survives a resize of the captured window, and accepts every current source. the capture toggle also lives per monitor in output stage. connect a spout sender. for a real vj rig: send a feed out of obs, resolume, touchdesigner or madmapper and receive it here at up to 60 fps. play one of your own video loops. no other app needed: add a file on the loops tab and play it, and every effect here runs on top of it. pick an effect while nothing is feeding ikandy and the app opens this same choice, the three doors plus preview anyway. the eleven capture fx time slits and time echo: time sculpture, with recorded beat ribbons and echoes of the feed. press, pixel press and glyph press: the print lab, the feed pressed into ink, pixels and glyphs. living paint and contour light: the feed's structure repainted, and traced in light. feedback cathedral, liquid glass, flow ink, and shatter and reform: retained highlights, refractive glass, source colored fluid motion, and spring driven fragments. each effect responds to kick, snare and hats with its own gestures instead of one generic pulse, and each keeps its intended color and retained state through the shared output pipeline, hdr included. the classic live-input scenes the same shelf carries the earlier spout effect scenes: live key for chroma and luma keying over a generated backdrop, datamosh, halftone, anamorphic, painterly, displace, slit scan, echo, kaleidoscope, feedback, glitch, pixelate, tunnel, edge, mirror, prism, liquid, ascii, vortex, heatwave, and a clean passthrough. good to know auto on the input shelf keeps rotating: an effect that cannot start moves on to the next. saved numbered presets, stage transitions and spout auto all work with capture fx, and switching effects repeatedly does not grow gpu memory. with a spout or ndi output attached, the show paces itself for that output at 4k instead of the console preview. tier note capture fx, screen and window capture, spout input and the video loop library ship in the studio tier, which is not on steam yet. spout output up to 30 fps is pro; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous fx shaders next → spout in + out

title: Spout in + out
desc: Publish visuals to OBS and VJ software, or post-process compatible feeds.
text: user guide / spout in + out spout in + out publish visuals to obs and vj software, or post-process compatible feeds. spout a node in the rig spout is a gpu texture-sharing workflow for compatible windows apps. ikandy supports spout input and output. spout out: publish the show turn on spout output in sources & settings, give the sender a name, and ikandy can appear as a source in compatible receivers such as obs, resolume, touchdesigner, madmapper, and vmix. the output is the composited visual feed; the console and panels are designed to stay out of it. output performance depends on your hardware, scene, resolution, and the receiving application. you can keep working in other apps while the feed runs. overlays on the broadcast two switches decide what rides on everything you broadcast, the second screen and spout and recordings alike: the now playing card and lyrics . one switch per overlay, so a clean feed is one click away. spout in: post-process a compatible feed pipe a live feed into ikandy from a compatible spout sender such as obs, touchdesigner, resolume, or madmapper: pick the sender in source → spout in , choose a frame rate up to 60, and use the feed as a source. the browser's spout tab contains scenes built for live feeds. tier note spout output up to 30 fps ships in the pro tier; 60 fps and above, spout input and ndi output ship in the studio tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous capture fx next → wallpaper + displays

title: Wallpaper + displays
desc: Any visual behind your icons. Mirror or Span, per display, survives Explorer restarts.
text: user guide / wallpaper + displays wallpaper + displays any visual behind your icons. mirror or span, per display, survives explorer restarts. set the desktop as your stage live wallpaper runs the visual behind your desktop icons while you work, on any mix of displays, driven by whatever ikandy is listening to. it is a set-and-forget output: open output stage , click a display on the monitor map, turn on wallpaper for it, and get back to work. change the visual any time from the console or stage and the desktop follows. the wallpaper survives explorer restarts, and it keeps rendering even when the main ikandy window is covered or minimized. fit mode: mirror or span mirror (the default) puts the same feed on each screen you picked. span stretches one image across all attached displays as a single canvas; it needs two or more screens, and it takes over the routing while it is on. both modes persist. the output window separate from wallpaper, the output window is a broadcast surface: mirror the main view onto the displays you choose, each mirror with its own gain, or span one continuous visual edge to edge (the titlebar hides so nothing interrupts the image). right-click the fullscreen button for a quick "send to a second screen" chooser. add hide-ui mode and the pixels are all that is left. overlays the now playing card and lyrics each have a broadcast switch: show them on the second screen, spout, and recordings, or keep every output clean. good to know toggle wallpaper off any time from the same panel if anything misbehaves. performance cost scales with the visual you pick. calm scenes cost very little; heavy compute scenes cost more. tier note desktop wallpaper ships in the pro tier, on any number of displays and in both fit modes. the output window on a single screen is also pro. spanning one visual across multiple monitors and running mirrors on several screens at once ship in the pro tier too (they moved down from studio in august 2026); see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous spout in + out next → loops + recording

title: Loops + recording
desc: Your own video loops as a layer in the show, plus F9 replay, Shift+F9 recording and bar-locked loop capture.
text: user guide / loops + recording loops + recording your own video loops as a layer in the show, plus f9 replay, shift+f9 recording and bar-locked loop capture. my loops the loops tab of the library is a video library of your own files. a loop plays as a feed on the show, so every capture fx and live-input effect can run on top of it. add and play open the library and the loops tab. press add video , or drop a video anywhere in the ikandy window. mp4, webm, mov, m4v and mkv are accepted; the file is copied into your library, deduplicated, and given a cover. click a loop to play it. the library closes, the playing canvas comes forward, and the input effects go to auto. each card has a favorite, a name and a bpm tag you can set. loops play muted: the reaction always comes from the audio source ikandy is listening to. loops do not join auto rotation on their own. a fresh install ships with one starter clip, a 30 second big buck bunny excerpt (blender foundation, cc by 3.0), so the library is never empty. hdr loops high bit depth video keeps its color and highlight range through loops, mix and the canvas, and image studio plays hdr loops natively. display p3 video keeps its gamut all the way to the screen. replay and record f9 saves the last 30 seconds. rolling replay keeps a buffer running in the background so f9 has those seconds. it is off by default because it costs some gpu, and pressing f9 turns it on for you. shift + f9 records from now until you press it again and saves the clip, whether or not replay is on. it pauses automatically when you turn on span, mirror or wallpaper. turning on spout or ndi output pauses the background replay recorder so the live feed stays smooth. press f9 again after the show if you want the replay back. in stage, the capture bank records 8, 16 or 32 bar loops locked to the live tempo. export settings in settings, output , beside the replay switch: export quality social (1080p at 60 frames per second, sized for social platforms) or master (the native render resolution and a much higher bitrate, for editing); export format mp4 (h.264 and aac, the one container instagram, tiktok and x all accept) or webm (vp9 and opus, encoded in software, so slower); recording dynamic range sdr, sdr 10 bit, hdr pq or hdr hlg; and the recording watermark switch. changing quality, format or range restarts the replay buffer. tier note f9 replay, shift+f9 recording and loop export are free for everyone, with a watermark on the clip; turning the watermark off is a studio feature. adding and playing video loops ships in the studio tier, which is not on steam yet; browsing the loop library is open at every tier. see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous wallpaper + displays next → lyrics

title: Lyrics
desc: Synced lyrics on screen, where they come from, and what to do when a track has none.
text: user guide / lyrics lyrics synced lyrics on screen, where they come from, and what to do when a track has none. lyrics words on the show synced lyrics ride the visuals, line by line, timed to the track. click the album art on the console to open them; click again to put them away. three modes classic draws the current line clean over the show. physics hands each line to a physics simulation, so words drift, swing, and settle with their own weight. make them yours position the line at the top, center, or bottom of the stage, scale the font from subtle to headline, set the opacity, and pick a color: the theme accent, white, or a swatch of your own. where the words come from ikandy reads lyrics from your own files, matched by the artist and title of the playing track: a synced .lrc file saved next to the track, or one in your linked lyrics folder. synced files scroll in time with the music; plain text shows as static lyrics. if no local file matches, ikandy shows nothing instead of guessing, which is where the next part comes in. add your own: tap to time open add lyrics and paste the words. if they already carry timestamps, they play immediately. if they are plain text, tap to time turns timing them into a performance: play the track and stamp each line the moment it lands. seekable sources get a small timeline with previous, play, and next, so a missed stamp is a two-second fix, not a restart. saved lyrics live in your local lyrics folder, keyed by title and artist, and you can point ikandy at a folder of your own. on the broadcast lyrics have their own broadcast switch: show them on the second screen, spout, and recordings , or keep the output clean. tier note physics lyrics and the tap-to-time editor ship in the pro tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous loops + recording next → stage: perform

title: STAGE: perform
desc: Now/Next decks, GO with crossfades, blackout and strobe, pads, rundowns, shows, combos.
text: user guide / stage: perform stage: perform now/next decks, go with crossfades, blackout and strobe, pads, rundowns, shows, combos. the console you perform from stage is the live view: a broadcast desk for planning a night and steering it in real time. when stage is live, the main window shows a return button so you always know which surface has control. now, next, go two decks with live previews: now is what the room sees, next is what you have lined up. click next to pick a look from the library, long-press to grab whatever is currently playing, right-click to clear. hit go and next takes the stage with a real crossfade: the outgoing frame freezes and dissolves into the incoming look, so transitions read as intentional, never as a cut. hold pins the current look against the autopilot. ride the moment a row of momentary performance keys sits under your fingers: blackout , a beat-locked strobe (hard photosensitive-safety cap of three flashes per second), and freeze . press and hold; release and the show returns. every stage control carries an address, so all of it lands on midi and osc . pads hot-cue pads hold looks you want on a trigger, each with a live thumbnail. assign a pad, hit it when the room needs it. rundowns, plans, pools, autopilot build a rundown for the night: concrete entries play a specific look with its own duration, pool entries shuffle from a group you curated. reorder by drag; unset entries flag themselves so nothing surprises you mid-set. autopilot follows the rundown, or smart-shuffles when none is loaded, with a dwell you pick from seconds to minutes and a live countdown to the next switch. shows new / save / load / delete manage whole shows: a saved show carries the rundown, your pads, and the per-output setup, so friday's rig comes back with one load. combos the combos tab is a layer compositor with a live preview: stack looks into a composite, save it, and recall the whole stack in one click. tempo and the logo tap four or more times to set the bpm by feel; double-click to clear it. the logo button opens the image studio to build or edit your overlay and lights up whenever one is live. outputs route per screen, so the projector and the stream can carry different dressing. stage ships in the studio tier. tier contents at launch are listed on the pricing page ; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous lyrics next → logo maker

title: Logo maker
desc: Image Studio: text or image, chrome and matte finishes, live on any visual.
text: user guide / logo maker logo maker image studio: text or image, chrome and matte finishes, live on any visual. image studio: make the logo the logo maker builds a broadcast-style overlay that rides on top of any running visual: your name, your mark, live on the output. create start from text or bring an image from your library. a studio preview backdrop helps you judge it, and it is preview only: your logo stays transparent and the backdrop is never baked into the asset. finishes two live material finishes ship today: chrome , liquid metal that catches the scene, and black , a matte powder-coat. each asset also carries its own audio-reactivity control, so the logo can breathe with the music or hold still. save and apply apply live puts it on the output immediately. save as new keeps a version; originals and templates are protected from overwrite. on stage, the logo button opens the studio directly and lights up whenever an overlay is live, so you always know it is on. ← previous stage: perform next → midi, phone remote, gamepad

title: MIDI, phone remote, gamepad
desc: Bind hardware with MIDI Learn, steer from your phone over LAN, fly with a controller.
text: user guide / midi, phone remote, gamepad midi, phone remote, gamepad bind hardware with midi learn, steer from your phone over lan, fly with a controller. hands on the rig three ways to drive ikandy without touching the mouse: hardware midi, your phone, and a game controller. midi learn click midi learn , then move a control on your hardware. that knob or fader is now bound. bindings can be exported and imported as json, so a rig setup travels with you. bound controls tick green so you can see the mapping land. osc stage carries an osc receiver: switch it on, set the port, and send. every stage control has a stable address (strobe, blackout, go, pads, and the rest), so lighting desks and show controllers speak to ikandy the same way your hardware does. phone remote (lan) start the phone remote and a phone on your local network can steer the show from its browser. this is intended for a trusted lan, not direct internet exposure. use the source-ip allowlist on shared or untrusted networks; leave it empty only when you intend to accept all local senders. gamepad flight flight scenes accept a controller with zero setup: plug one in and any input takes the controls. left stick steers, right stick looks, right trigger throttle, left trigger brake. hands off for five seconds and the autopilot resumes; tab or the b button hands back instantly. the mouse never touches the camera, it belongs to the ui. midi and osc control ship in the studio tier. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous logo maker next → shader import + reactivity

title: AI scene generation
desc: Bring your own key. Generate, fix, and tune scenes with a supported provider.
text: user guide / ai scene generation ai scene generation bring your own key. generate, fix, and tune scenes with a supported provider. an ai that writes scenes ikandy can generate new visual scenes with ai, and can repair or tune imported shaders in the ai shader studio. it is bring-your-own-key: you connect an account from a supported provider and pay that provider directly. ikandy does not sell separate ai credits. your key stays yours the credential is stored using the operating system's secure storage. ikandy uses it to authenticate requests to the provider you choose; provider terms and data handling apply. what it can do generate : describe a look and get a runnable scene. ai fix : paste a shader that will not compile and let the sandbox suggest a repair after a compile check. ai tune : ask for adjustments to a working scene, in plain language. costs provider charges, availability, and estimates can change. review the estimate shown in ikandy and your provider's terms before you submit a job. guided ai scene generation ships in the pro tier. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous shader import + reactivity next → steam workshop

title: Steam Workshop
desc: Publish scenes you made, pull in what other players made, and keep your name on the work.
text: user guide / steam workshop steam workshop publish scenes you made, pull in what other players made, and keep your name on the work. the workshop shelf the library's workshop shelf browses everything the community has published, straight from the steam workshop, without leaving the app. browse and download open the library and choose workshop on the rail. search, filter by everything, ai art, shader works or downloaded, and sort by trending, newest or most subscribed. every card says where the item will land before you take it: ai art lands in my scenes under its own vibe, and shader works land in artists under their maker's name. press download . ikandy subscribes to the item on steam and files it for you. the subscribed tab of the workshop panel lists what you have taken, and workshop items enter the finishing chain like every other scene. publish your work launch ikandy through steam: publishing needs the steam client. on the workshop shelf press publish your work , or open the workshop panel from the my scenes header. choose the scene, give it a title and a description, and pick who it publishes as: your steam name or your ikandy handle. shader credits and filenames always use the ikandy handle. tick the rights box, press publish to workshop , and accept steam's one-time workshop legal agreement, or the item stays hidden. items are tagged by how they were made and published as public, with a preview image generated for you. renaming a scene later keeps its identity, so the workshop preview does not go missing. preset packs outside the workshop, .ikpack files export a scene as a verified package you can share by hand and import on another pc. verified shadertoy imports carry a sealed provenance receipt, so an import that was tampered with cannot pass as the original. tier note browsing the workshop is free. downloading, publishing and .ikpack export ship in the pro tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous ai scene generation next → games

title: Games
desc: One Small Step, a shared moon that dances to everyone's music, and Slingshot, a gravity-well melee. Both free.
text: user guide / games games one small step, a shared moon that dances to everyone's music, and slingshot, a gravity-well melee. both free. the game tab open the library and pick game. one small step and slingshot live there. a gamepad is the way to play both, and slingshot also works on the keyboard. pilot and auto never rotate away from a running game. one small step a shared moon. everyone on it hears their own music, and the moon turns all of it into one sky. you drive a rover across lunar terrain, jump craters, transform into a plane, and hang out at the drive in, where the screen plays visuals to your soundtrack on a 15 second cycle. other players appear as lights, each in their own permanent color, pulsing at the tempo of whatever they are listening to. the first time you arrive, the moon asks one question: join the shared moon , or play solo . joining is free and shares your handle and rover position while you play. you can show up as your ikandy name or your steam name, and switch later in settings under privacy. change your mind any time with the solo or shared chip at the top of the moon, or the shared moon switch in settings. press c for the controller map. a jumps, y transforms to the plane, b fires a paint comet, m opens the radar map, g opens the gif tray, and a click of the right stick opens and sends a gif. on the d-pad: up for the gif tray, down for a greeting flash, left for the palette, right for a waypoint. your music is your paint. fire a comet during a drop and it paints a fat blazing ribbon; in a quiet bridge, a thin filament. the sky keeps the day's paintings and they fade slowly over hours, so someone arriving late inherits the sky everyone else made. fly like you mean it. jump, then jump again with the stick held: side throws a barrel roll, back a backflip, forward a front flip, with full air control on the sticks. other players see every flip. six mini games: drop chasing, prospecting, groove runs, trick sessions, constellation raising and canvas flats. crystals: park close and hold through the beats. rings: pass them in order on the pulse. the boneyard rewards air tricks. four points of interest: earthrise overlook, prism springs, the boneyard and tranquility ring. the handshake. flash your headlights at someone. if they flash back within a few seconds, an arc of light in both your colors bridges your rovers. sparks and the rover shop. earn sparks through play and spend them on light rigs, trail tints and horn chimes that nearby players can see and hear. every gif plays its sender's horn chime; a gif sounds switch in settings keeps the moon silent. slingshot a modern gravity-well melee. build a fleet from 25 ships on a 200 point budget, five distinct hulls per fleet with a reserve switch, and fight around a planet whose gravity well is the arena. the nebula paints the live spectrum and the well pulses on the beat. solo against easy, medium or hard bots. two players on one keyboard. online, with picks sealed until both players are ready and a ready-up showdown. both players need the same ikandy version; the lobby says so instead of desyncing. xbox pattern controllers throughout. enter or space selects, backspace goes back, and a launch bar ends fleet building. the match is a fixed step simulation with checksums, so a tampered client can only void a match, never win it. slingshot's clean stage puts the pets away. tier note joining the moon, driving, flying, painting, the mini games, cosmetics and slingshot in every mode are free. sending a gif on the moon is a pro feature; receiving them is free. see pricing . ← previous steam workshop next → pets

title: Pets
desc: Five companions who live on the show and dance to the tempo of your music. Free for everyone.
text: user guide / pets pets five companions who live on the show and dance to the tempo of your music. free for everyone. who is out four cats, fruitbat, hobbes, suki and pixel, each with their own personality, and cooper, a blue merle aussie puppy. one cat at a time; cooper can join whoever is out, or run solo. pick a companion middle-click anywhere, or press q , to open the shortcuts wheel of the quick access ring, then pick pets . shift plus right-click opens the same wheel for a mouse without a middle button. choose off, fruitbat, hobbes, suki, pixel or cooper. the choice persists. play with them click a pet to say hello. drag to carry. they always land on their feet. double-click to feed a treat. throw the ball for cooper: throw, bounce, chase, retrieve, return. he will bring it back. always. wiggle the mouse near a cat and watch what happens. each pet has ten dance styles keyed to the live tempo of your music, and its own show commentary. they walk across the whole screen, including the console bar. on every output pets live on the show itself, so mirrors, recordings, spout, ndi and the wallpaper all see them, at native resolution on 4k output. they stay out when you hide the ui, because hide ui clears the controls, not the show. slingshot's clean stage puts them away. cost having a pet out is cheap: the pet layer is capped at 30 frames per second and uploads only the region it draws. if frames matter more than company, choose off. tier note pets are free for everyone. ← previous games next → controls, themes, tips

title: Controls, themes, tips
desc: Reactivity, seek and volume, three theme layers, UI size, workflow tips.
text: user guide / controls, themes, tips controls, themes, tips reactivity, seek and volume, three theme layers, ui size, workflow tips. controls & themes tune the whole thing the console is the control surface; this page is the small print around it. reactivity, everywhere it matters every engine carries a reactivity control: turn it down and the visuals settle into calm ambient motion, turn it up and they snap to the beat. the master audio popover goes further with bass, mid, and treble drive , a mix control, and the master intensity fader. sensible defaults sit in the middle and work for most music. the seek bar the progress bar in the playback zone is draggable: click and drag anywhere on it to seek, on every source that supports seeking. volume lives right next to it for sources that allow control; anything that does not is greyed with a hint, not hidden. three layers of theme console material : black , a matte powder-coat, or chrome , liquid metal with dark text. the whole board, browser, and playlist panel change together. accent color : swatches like gold, neon, forest, ember, lavender, and crimson, plus a custom picker and a random that surprises you. the accent runs through every knob, tab, and led. panel background : schemes including slate and the light cloud, plus a panel opacity slider so the chrome can float over the show as much or as little as you like. add the knobs / sliders switch for how the board's controls render, and a ui size setting for readability at couch distance. themes change the chrome, never the visuals. set it once, forget it everything persists across sessions: reactivity, theme, accent, source preferences, custom preset folders, the last-used look. close it, reopen it, it is your rig. workflow tips spotlight a scene or image : drop the milkdrop opacity in its settings popover to 30 to 50 percent and let the layer underneath breathe through. scenes and fx shaders run at the same time. for recording or streaming : classic lyric mode over a clean scene with a subtle analog fx reads beautifully on video, and the broadcast overlay switches keep the feed intentional. lyrics need honest metadata : correct artist and title fetch the right words. if lyrics look wrong, check the tags on the playing source first. ← previous pets next → troubleshooting + help

title: Troubleshooting + help
desc: Fixes for the common snags, and where to reach a human.
text: user guide / troubleshooting + help troubleshooting + help fixes for the common snags, and where to reach a human. troubleshooting when things get weird the most common issues people run into, and how to fix them. click any item to expand. now playing says "nothing is playing" windows reports no app is currently registered as the smtc owner. simply start playing music in any app and the message will disappear within a second. if music is playing and now playing still doesn’t see it: firefox : open about:config , set media.hardwaremediakeys.enabled to true , restart firefox. chrome / edge : check chrome://flags for hardware media key handling and set it to enabled . apple music for windows : can be inconsistent. try pausing/resuming, or use a dedicated source instead. now playing controls grey out / next or previous don't work by design. ikandy queries the active app for which transport commands it actually exposes: some apps (single youtube videos, podcasts) don’t advertise next or previous, so ikandy locks those buttons. hover any greyed-out button to see the reason. for broader transport controls, connect a dedicated source such as musicbee, foobar2000, or vlc, or play in an app that publishes full controls to windows media controls. "could not start audio source" / no audio reactivity windows treats system audio capture the same as microphone access for privacy purposes. fix: settings → privacy & security → microphone → toggle let desktop apps access your microphone on. restart ikandy. if that doesn’t help, click 🎤 reconnect audio in settings (⚙) → source tab . spotify: which controls work? spotify plays through windows media controls. play, pause, and skip work when spotify publishes them; some controls (seek, volume, shuffle) live inside spotify itself. there is no sign-in and no account connection: press play in spotify and ikandy follows. if you followed an older guide that asked for a client id and a spotify developer app, that connection has been removed from ikandy. no setup is needed anymore. vlc won't connect open http://localhost:8080 in a browser: you should see the vlc web ui password prompt. if you don't, the web interface isn't enabled. fix: vlc → tools → preferences → show settings: all → interface → main interfaces → tick web . expand lua below it and confirm a lua http password is set. restart vlc. foobar2000 won't connect in foobar2000 → file → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control , confirm enable http server is ticked. test by visiting http://localhost:8880 in a browser. if you see the beefweb player, the plugin is healthy. if you set a password, paste it exactly as configured in ikandy's foobar2000 settings. musicbee won't connect confirm musicbee is running and that mbxhub appears under edit → preferences → plugins . the mbxhub bundle's mb_mbxhub.dll and mbxhub.exe should be in musicbee's plugins folder. test by visiting http://localhost:8080/docs in a browser. if the mbxhub api documentation loads, match ikandy's host and port to the plugin configuration. the ikandy defaults are 127.0.0.1 and 8080 . if the plugin does not load, confirm .net framework 4.8 and the .net 8 desktop runtime are available, then check the official mbxhub requirements and installation notes . for help with mbxhub itself (installing it, the plugin not loading, its settings), ask in the mbxhub support thread on the musicbee forum . if mbxhub is running and ikandy still won't connect, email support@ikandy.app . install or update problems through steam steam handles installing and updating ikandy. if an install stalls or a launch fails after an update, use steam's built-in repair: right-click ikandy in your library, then properties → installed files → verify integrity of game files . why doesn't ikandy react only to spotify or musicbee when i'm playing a game? by default ikandy captures the entire system audio mix: game sound effects, discord calls, notification pings, and music all go in together. the visualizer reacts to whichever is loudest at any given moment, which is often the game. fix: use per-process capture. open settings (⚙) → source tab → per-process capture , click scan , then click capture next to spotify or musicbee. ikandy will focus on that app's audio stream while the game keeps running normally. visuals don't react to my music confirm the source is connected: the console bar's now playing zone should show the track name and source. visuals react to system audio regardless of which source you’ve picked for track info. if the visualizer is static while music plays, audio isn’t reaching ikandy. click 🎤 reconnect audio in settings (⚙) → source tab , and check windows microphone permissions. i have 5.1 or 7.1 surround sound and the visuals barely move ikandy captures a stereo loopback stream. with 5.1/7.1 configured, windows mixes most music into rear/centre/sub channels, leaving the front l/r that ikandy captures very quiet. fix: set your default output to stereo (2 channel) : right-click speaker icon → sounds → playback tab. right-click your active output → configure speakers → choose stereo . right-click again → properties → advanced → pick a 2-channel format from default format . apply, then in ikandy hit 🎤 reconnect audio in settings (⚙) → source tab . lyrics aren't showing up lyrics load from your own files, matched by the artist and title of the playing track: a synced .lrc next to the track, or one in your linked lyrics folder. if no local file matches, ikandy shows nothing instead of guessing. use add lyrics and tap to time to create one; see the lyrics guide . also check: if your files have incorrect artist/title tags, the match can land on the wrong song. performance is choppy or stuttering ikandy is gpu-bound. if your gpu is busy with another task, frame rate will suffer. try: lower reactivity in the master audio popover, drop the milkdrop opacity in its settings popover, or step the quality tier down; pick a simpler scene (spectrum or aurora instead of starfield); or open the image tab and disable fx shaders to remove a full-frame post-process pass. on laptops, make sure ikandy is using the discrete gpu: settings → system → display → graphics . the app won't launch / crashes on startup try a clean reinstall: uninstall via settings → apps, delete %appdata%\ikandy , then reinstall the latest build. if it still crashes, email support@ikandy.app with your windows version, gpu, and any error message shown. where are my settings stored? ikandy stores all user data in the electron userdata folder: %appdata%\ikandy (paste into the explorer address bar). files stored there include source preferences, preset reactivity scores, favorites, hidden presets, and thumbnail cache. uninstall note: the standard nsis uninstaller on windows does not delete %appdata%\ikandy . your settings, favorites, and cached thumbnails survive an uninstall and are picked up automatically when you reinstall. to fully reset ikandy, delete that folder manually after uninstalling. get help stuck? reach out. discord for chat and quick answers, email for bugs, coffee if it made your day. 💬 discord 🐛 report a bug ☕ support ← previous controls, themes, tips

title: Shader import + reactivity
desc: Paste a shader, drive it from the music. Three layers, in the order to reach for them: the knobs that already exist, your own knobs from one comment block, then the audio uniforms read straight from your code. None of it needs an AI key.
text: user guide / shader import + reactivity shader import + reactivity paste a shader, drive it from the music. three layers, in the order to reach for them: the knobs that already exist, your own knobs from one comment block, then the audio uniforms read straight from your code. none of it needs an ai key. layer one: the knobs you already have open the console. these act on whatever is on screen right now, imported shaders included, with no editing and no reload. bass 0 – 2 · starts at 1 multiplies the low band before your shader sees it. mid 0 – 2 · starts at 1 same, for the middle band. treble 0 – 2 · starts at 1 same, for the top band. smooth 0.30 – 0.98 · starts at 0.40 higher glides, lower twitches. one global analyser setting. intensity 1 – 11 · starts at 8 the big fader. multiplies all three bands on top of the knobs above. speed 0.1 – 2 · starts at 1 scales the scene clock for imported glsl. never touches the music. they stack, and the stacking is the part most people miss: what your shader actually receives u_bass = rawbass × bass knob (0–2) × intensity (0–2) the intensity fader reads 1 to 11 on screen but drives 0 to 2 underneath: display 6 is 1.0× , display 11 is 2.0× , and the default display 8 is 1.4× . a factory-fresh ikandy is already feeding your shader 1.4 times what it was written for. want more? bass at 2 with intensity at 11 gives you 4× the raw band, roughly three times the default. that is the ceiling from the console alone. want it dead still? intensity at 1 sends every band to exactly zero. that is deliberate: it is the defeat switch, not a low setting. bass, mid and treble are saved per engine, so your imported-shader settings do not follow you into milkdrop. intensity is one global value. the reactivity section two of its four knobs act on an imported shader: light-sync (starts at 85%) lets the beat drive brightness and glow in the post chain. fx pulse (starts at 50%) lets hits pump the bloom, chromatic aberration and vignette for a moment. motion warp and transform start at zero and stay inert on glsl and webgpu by design. see colour, zoom, and the motion rule . layer two: your own knobs, one comment block put a single line comment in your pasted source and ikandy builds you real knobs in the console's scene section: sliders, toggles, dropdowns, a proper colour picker. they persist with the scene and come back when it reloads. // ikandy-controls: [ // {"id":"glow", "label":"glow", "type":"float", "range":[0,2], "default":0.8, "mapsto":"u_glow"}, // {"id":"tint", "label":"tint", "type":"color", "default":"#66ccff", "mapsto":"u_tint"}, // {"id":"spin", "label":"spin", "type":"bool", "default":true, "mapsto":"u_spin"} // ] void mainimage(out vec4 fragcolor, in vec2 fragcoord) { vec2 uv = fragcoord / iresolution.xy; vec3 col = u_tint * smoothstep(0.8, 0.0, length(uv - 0.5)); col *= 1.0 + u_glow * u_basss; // your knob, times the music fragcolor = vec4(col, 1.0); } put it anywhere in the pasted source. on a multipass shader it goes in the common tab, or the top of image if you have no common tab, and every pass can read the uniform. four rules that will bite you do not declare the uniform yourself. ikandy writes uniform float u_glow; for you. adding your own is a redefinition error, and you get a message telling you to delete the line. read it or lose it. a control that is declared but never actually read in the code is dropped, and the load status names it. no dead knobs. reading it inside a comment does not count, because comments are stripped before the check. one block per shader. a second block is an error, not a merge. a malformed block stops the load and tells you the block line and the source line. it never quietly gives you zero knobs. fields field needed what it does mapsto yes the uniform name: u_ plus letters, digits, underscore. cannot be a built-in like u_bass . label should the name on the knob. type should float (knob, the default), int , color (picker, arrives as a vec3), bool (toggle), enum (dropdown, needs options ). range float / int [min, max] default should starting value. colours take "#rrggbb" or [r,g,b] in 0–1. id should short key used for saving. defaults to mapsto . options enum [{"value":0,"label":"soft"}, ...] audiodefault no wires the knob to a band. see below. up to 12 controls. duplicate or reserved mapsto names are dropped, with the reason logged to the developer console. in a wgsl import you read uc.glow inside fs_main , which is your mapsto with the u_ prefix removed. everything else is identical. point a knob at a band this is the direct answer to “how do i put the bass on something else?” add audiodefault to any float or int control and that knob is modulated by the band every frame, without touching your shader code. // ikandy-controls: [ // {"id":"zoom", "label":"zoom", "type":"float", "range":[0.5,3], "default":1.0, // "mapsto":"u_zoom", "audiodefault" : {"band": "bass" , "gain":1.5}}, // // {"id":"hue", "label":"hue", "type":"float", "range":[0,1], "default":0.2, // "mapsto":"u_hue", "audiodefault" : {"band": "treble" , "gain":0.6}} // ] how the value is computed each frame value = knob position × (1 + band × gain) bands are bass , mid , treble and volume . gain is clamped to 0–8. the knob you set by hand stays the base, so you keep a manual trim on top of the music. repointing it live, without editing you can move a control from one band to another while the shader runs: load the shader, then save it. reopen it from the my scenes dropdown with open , in the same panel. every float and int control now shows a small pill under its name: off, bass, mid, treble, volume. pick one. it applies immediately and is remembered. the pill appears only on a shader the panel itself opened, which is why the save-then-open step matters. loading a fresh paste gives you the knobs but not the pills. one more thing worth knowing: if you later edit the ikandy-controls block in the saved file, the file wins over the remembered pill settings on the next load. layer three: straight into the source the fastest loop. the paste box is the editor: type in it and press ctrl+enter to recompile. ikandy declares all of these for you, so just read them. uniform what it carries u_bass u_mid u_treble the three bands, after your console knobs and intensity. fast and spiky. u_basss u_mids u_trebs the same bands, envelope-smoothed. use these for anything that should glide. u_kicktight the kick drum transient, 50–110 hz. the structural pulse. u_snare backbeat body and crack. good for colour and saturation flares. u_hihat 6–16 khz tick. fast, fine sparkle. u_subbass 20–60 hz rumble. slow glow and depth. u_air 16–22 khz sheen. slow shimmer. u_basshit u_midhit u_trebhit raw onset envelopes per band. u_buildup u_peak u_calm u_release u_sustain u_arc song shape. these rise and fall over seconds, not beats. stage the drop with them. u_beat u_beatphase u_barphase u_bpm the live beat clock. u_drive the intensity fader itself, 0–2. multiply your reactivity by it so your shader goes fully still at zero. u_volume u_intensity overall loudness. u_volume is the rms of the bands, u_intensity is their mean. spectrumat(x) waveformat(x) helper functions. sample the full spectrum or waveform; x and the result are both 0–1. shadertoy shaders work unchanged. every ichannel resolves to ikandy's live audio in the exact 512×2 texture format shadertoy uses: fft on one row, waveform on the other. a shader that already samples a music channel reacts the moment it loads, with nothing to press. iresolution , imouse , idate , iframe and the rest are wired too. shadertoy library textures do not travel with an export, so bind your own image or the shader renders without them. the one audio-driven camera, zoom or geometry bindings. the reason is motion comfort. repetitive whole-field movement in roughly the 0.08 to 0.5 hz band is what makes people queasy, and music sitting at 100 to 140 bpm puts a bass-driven zoom uncomfortably close to it. if you want breathing zoom, write it yourself, keep the amplitude small, and watch it on a big screen for a few minutes before you put it
